summary_paragraph: Mrs. ___ was admitted with abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and odynophagia, following a recent hospitalization for respiratory symptoms. She has a complex history including prior tracheal cancer treated with radiation, which likely contributed to esophageal stricture and ulceration. A barium swallow revealed a 3 cm esophageal stricture that prevented passage of a 12-mm tablet, and EGD confirmed severe radiation-related esophagitis with an ulcer and nodule, both biopsied. Due to inflammation, dilation was deferred. She was treated empirically for candidal esophagitis with fluconazole and started on high-dose pantoprazole. Her viral upper respiratory infection resolved with supportive care, and her abdominal symptoms improved with antiemetics and bowel management. Prednisone was adjusted for rheumatoid arthritis flare, and her asthma, heart failure, and hypertension were managed. She was discharged home with services on a prednisone taper, pantoprazole, fluconazole, and follow-up plans for biopsy results and GI reevaluation.
